title: Index items by a key, keeping each item itself as the value

blocks.text: `Function.identity()` is the function `t -> t`: it returns its input **itself**, not a copy. Its classic use is as the value mapper of `Collectors.toMap`, when the value should be the stream element.
Write `Index.indexBy(List<T> items, Function<T, K> key)`. It returns a map from `key.apply(item)` to `item`; `Collectors.toMap` with `Function.identity()` is the page's way to build it.
Two items may produce the same key; keep the first. The map must iterate its keys in the order they first appear in `items`: a key seen again later keeps its first position.

cases.says: Each item is stored under its key, and the value is the item itself, not a copy.
When two items share a key, the first one is kept instead of failing on a duplicate key.
The map iterates its keys in the order they first appear in the list.
Keys are compared with equals, so two equal keys computed separately are one key.
A key that turns up again later stays where it first appeared in the order.

concepts: Function.identity() returns its input itself, not a copy, which makes it the natural value mapper for toMap.
